model_card.detail: Nyra Verbatim Speech Benchmark disfluency F1 and TIMIT word-boundary error; no LibriSpeech number reported for 2.0

reference_code.detail: MIT-licensed. crisperwhisper/{prompt,transformers_engine,word_timing,features,hallucination,fallback}.py and crisperwhisper/longform/* define the full decode contract; there is NO modeling file — the graph is stock transformers Whisper loaded via AutoModelForSpeechSeq2Seq

paper.detail: CrisperWhisper 2.0 paper referenced from the model card; not read for this intake

dtype.evidence: config.dtype=bfloat16; safetensors header is uniformly BF16 across all 481 tensors (no F32 norms/biases). Same for medium, large, and turbo.

upstream_benchmarks.notes: Disfluency F1, higher is better. Reported for 'CrisperWhisper 2.0' as a line, not per size; the model card does not break the number down by small/medium/large/turbo. English and German use human-labeled sets, the other eight languages use synthetic verbatim sets.
Mean absolute word-boundary error in milliseconds, lower is better. Scored only over words the system gets right. Reported for 'CrisperWhisper 2.0', not per size.

NOT REPORTED for CrisperWhisper 2.0. The publisher benchmarks disfluency F1 and word-boundary error, not standard WER. Recorded as null so the acceptance dataset stays visible; the Stage 7 gate uses the measured Oracle reference baseline. Sign-off decision (2026-08-07): report both mode=intended (standard normalizer) and mode=verbatim (normalizer additionally strips the 15 bracketed vocal-event tokens), and gate only on the intended number.

CONTEXT ONLY — this is CrisperWhisper v1 (nyrahealth/CrisperWhisper, a whisper-large-v2 finetune, deprecated), not 2.0. Open ASR Leaderboard entry dated 2024-08-29, normalized WER. Included to give an order of magnitude for a verbatim Whisper finetune under the leaderboard's text normalizer.

reference_rationale: The publisher ships `crisperwhisper` (PyPI, MIT, https://github.com/nyrahealth/CrisperWhisper) as the documented and only entrypoint, and the model card sets library_name=crisperwhisper. That package contains no modeling code: the graph is stock `transformers` Whisper, loaded via `AutoModelForSpeechSeq2Seq.from_pretrained(..., attn_implementation='eager')` (the `WhisperForConditionalGenerationWithAttentionLoss` string in config.architectures is a training-time subclass that appears nowhere in the inference package and is never resolved — Auto classes dispatch on model_type='whisper'). What the package DOES own is the entire decode contract: the `[verbatim_N]`/`[intended_N]` prompt-tag prefix, `<ctx>`/`<htx>`/`<vtx>` prompt markers, the always-`<|notimestamps|>` decoder prefix, the Viterbi word-timing aligner over supervised cross-attention heads, `<ctx>`-based continuation longform, temperature fallback, early-EOT recovery, and rewind/escape hallucination repair. Plain `transformers` alone reproduces the tensors but not the model's advertised behavior, so it cannot be the reference. The package's `TransformersEngine` is pure-torch, single-threadable, and already runs with eager attention, so it is directly instrumentable for Stage 2 dumps and lets us reuse scripts/dump_reference_whisper_transformers.py for the encoder/decoder tensor path while taking prompts and post-processing from the author package. CTranslate2 (`ctranslate2-crisperwhisper`, the fast path) is NOT the reference: it is a Linux-only CUDA fork with int8/fp16 fused kernels and speculative decoding, and the DOCS explicitly warn about fp16 batched-GEMM rounding divergence between the two backends.
known_risks: FRONTEND IS STOCK WHISPER, INCLUDING ITS NON-STANDARD COMPRESSION: no statistical normalization is applied (hence frontend.normalization='none'), but the mel is followed by Whisper's per-utterance dynamic-range compression `log10(clip(mel, 1e-10)) -> max(x, x.max() - 8.0) -> (x + 4.0) / 4.0`. The publisher's CT2 path vendors faster-whisper 1.2.1's numpy FeatureExtractor (crisperwhisper/features.py) and the transformers path uses AutoProcessor/WhisperFeatureExtractor; both are bit-comparable to what our whisper family already implements, so the frontend is the one part that ports over unchanged.

FAMILY SHAPE: 'just size variants' is only true for small/medium/large. small (d_model 768, 12+12 layers), medium (1024, 24+24), and large (1280, 32+32) are whisper-v2-generation derivatives: 80 mel bins, 99 language tokens, vocab_size 51896. turbo is a whisper-large-v3-turbo derivative: 128 mel bins, 100 language tokens (adds <|yue|>), vocab_size 51897, and 4 decoder layers against a 32-layer encoder. EVERY special-token id above 50357 shifts by +1 on turbo (<|transcribe|> 50359 vs 50360, <|notimestamps|> 50363 vs 50364, timestamp base 50364 vs 50365, [UM] 51865 vs 51866). turbo also ships begin_suppress_tokens=[220,50256] and forced_decoder_ids=null where the others ship forced_decoder_ids=[[1,50259],[2,50359]] and begin_suppress_tokens=null. Nothing may hardcode a token id; all ids must be read from generation_config/tokenizer per variant.

LICENSE: the weights are under the nyra health Non-Commercial Research License v1.0, NOT Apache-2.0 like openai/whisper. Non-Commercial Use only; the restriction extends to Outputs (Sec. 4) and inherits share-alike to Derivative Works (Sec. 3.1-3.2), which a converted GGUF is. Redistribution is permitted for Non-Commercial Use but Sec. 3.3 requires (a) shipping a complete copy of the agreement, (b) contractually binding recipients before or upon access, and (c) a NOTICE file with the prescribed attribution text. (b) effectively means any handy-computer/* GGUF repo must be gated, not just private. The `_pro` variants (small_pro/medium_pro/large_pro/turbo_pro) are gated:manual with no README and are commercial-license-only — out of scope. The inference code we read is MIT (Part A) and imposes nothing.

DECODE CONTRACT IS NOT WHISPER'S: the model is always decoded with the <|notimestamps|> prefix and never emits timestamp tokens. Segment timestamps and the whisper timestamp-token/`condition_on_prev_tokens` long-form stitching that our whisper family implements DO NOT APPLY and must not be reused. Timing comes exclusively from a Viterbi alignment over supervised cross-attention (crisperwhisper/word_timing.py, ~23 KB) using generation_config.alignment_heads plus a mel-energy-derived blank state; long-form comes from `<ctx> last N words <ectx>` continuation over 30 s windows at a 26 s stride (crisperwhisper/longform/continuation.py, ~25 KB).

PROMPT PREFIX ORDERING: the mode tags precede the Whisper prefix, not follow it, and there is no <|startofprev|> wrapper. The decoder input is literally `encode('[verbatim_1]...[verbatim_5]' [+ ' <ctx> ctx words <ectx>'] [+ ' <htx> hotwords <ehtx>']) + [<|sot|>, <|lang|>, <|transcribe|>, <|notimestamps|>]` (crisperwhisper/prompt.py). Context comes BEFORE hotwords because that is the training order. Getting this order wrong silently changes the output rather than erroring.

31 NON-SPECIAL ADDED TOKENS: ids 51865-51895 (51866-51896 on turbo) are 15 vocal-event tokens ([UM],[UH],[laughter],[sniff],[throatclearing],[cough],[sigh],[breath],[lipsmack],[yawn],[noise],[crying],[fart],[scream],[sneeze]), 5 [verbatim_N], 5 [intended_N], and 6 markers (<vtx>,<evtx>,<ctx>,<ectx>,<htx>,<ehtx>). All carry special=false in tokenizer.json, so skip_special_tokens does NOT strip them; the reference filters them by explicit id list plus regex (prompt.strip_prompt_artifacts). The vocal-event tokens are intended output and must survive; the mode/marker tokens must be stripped. The converter must export the full added-token list or the rebuilt tokenizer will not cover the model's 51896-wide output space.

BASE BPE VOCAB IS UNCHANGED: vocab_sha256 c48834...ec6d is byte-identical to openai/whisper-small's, so vocab.json/merges.txt need no new handling; only added_tokens differ. This is a v2-model property — CrisperWhisper v1 (nyrahealth/CrisperWhisper) shipped a genuinely 'changed tokenizer' with remapped special-token strings, which the reference still special-cases. Do not port v1.

DTYPE: uniformly BF16 including norms and biases (481/481 tensors), unlike every openai/whisper checkpoint (F32 for tiny..large-v2, F16 for large-v3). scripts/convert-whisper.py already has a BF16 branch (MOSTLY_BF16) that demotes the conv stem to F16 because the loader has no BF16 conv kernel — that demotion is now on the accuracy-reference path, not an edge case, and must be re-justified against reference drift rather than inherited.

REFERENCE HARNESS DISABLES HF DEFAULTS: TransformersEngine sets generation_config.forced_decoder_ids=None and begin_suppress_tokens=None at load, and always passes an explicit resolved suppress_tokens list (an explicit [] must DISABLE suppression, not fall back to the config default). Any Stage 2 dump that lets HF apply its own forced ids or begin-suppression will diverge from the publisher's harness on the first decoded token.

LANGUAGE SCOPE VS CLAIM: the checkpoint carries all 99 (100 on turbo) Whisper language tokens and generation_config keeps forced_decoder_ids=[[1,null]] (HF's language-detection marker), but the model card declares only en+de and the published benchmark covers 10 languages. Language detection is inherited from Whisper and is neither exercised nor claimed by the author harness (transcribe() takes language='en' as a default and always forces a lang token). Detection quality on a verbatim finetune is unmeasured.

TRANSLATION IS INHERITED BUT UNVALIDATED: generation_config.task_to_id still contains translate=50358 and the <|translate|> token is in the vocab, but the author package exposes no translate path (get_decoder_prefix hardcodes transcribe_id) and neither the card nor DOCS.md mentions translation.

WER GATE SEMANTICS: default mode is 'verbatim', which by design emits [UM]/[UH]/[laughter]/... and preserves stutters and false starts. Scored against LibriSpeech's clean references with the standard normalizer this inflates WER for correct behavior. The Stage 7 WER gate must either run mode='intended' or normalize the bracketed event tokens away, and the choice must be identical for the Oracle reference baseline and the C++ run.

DECODE-LOOP FEATURES ON BY DEFAULT: transcribe() defaults hallucination_mitigation=True (rewind/escape repair, crisperwhisper/hallucination.py ~20 KB), early_eot_recovery=True (bans EOT for min_new_tokens and measures stop_prob), and temperature_fallback=True (collapse recovery). Reference dumps and any C++ parity target must pin these explicitly; leaving them at their defaults makes greedy-argmax parity untestable because the reference may rewind and re-decode.

max_new_tokens DEFAULTS TO 256, not max_target_positions=448. Prompt tokens consume decoder positions ahead of generation ([verbatim_1..5] alone is 5+ tokens; a 12-word <ctx> block adds ~15 more), so the usable generation budget per 30 s window is smaller than vanilla Whisper's and shrinks as context grows. The 448 position limit is a hard cap that prompt + context + output must jointly respect.

HOTWORDS ARE PRO-ONLY: the <htx>/<ehtx> path exists in the tokenizer and prompt builder for every checkpoint, but the standard (non-pro) models were never trained with hotword prompts and the reference raises a UserWarning and warns of degradation. Do not implement or validate hotword biasing against a non-pro checkpoint.

intake_gaps.reason: left null. <|translate|> (50358) and task_to_id.translate survive in the checkpoint, but the publisher's package exposes no translate path and neither the model card nor DOCS.md claims translation. Inherited-but-unvalidated; resolve by measurement at Stage 2 or accept as OUT OF SCOPE at sign-off.

declared as the full 99 Whisper language codes (what the tokenizer and generation_config.lang_to_id actually carry and what the runtime must accept for --language). The model card declares only en+de and the published benchmark covers 10 languages. Accepted deliberately so GGUF general.languages is not narrower than the checkpoint; per-language accuracy beyond en/de is unmeasured.

declared true on mechanism evidence (99 <|lang|> tokens plus generation_config.forced_decoder_ids=[[1,null]], HF's detect-language marker). The author reference harness never exercises it, so the Stage 2 reference for this capability has to be stock transformers generate(language=None) rather than crisperwhisper.transcribe().

RESOLVED at intake sign-off (2026-08-07): non-commercial research license with share-alike and a contractual-binding redistribution clause (Sec 3.3(b)). Maintainer decision is to port and ship C++ support but publish NO GGUF for this family; users convert their own checkpoints locally. No distribution means Sec 3.3 does not attach. The Non-Commercial restriction on Outputs (Sec 4) still binds our own use of transcripts, including as training data.
